artifacts.summary: Implementation summary: converged /todo roadmap annotation with roadmap-integration.sh parse-only/filtered-annotate design across both /todo specs

completion_data.completion_summary: Made roadmap-integration.sh /todo's single parser and structure-signal source (parse-only scan + --annotate against a pre-archival filtered snapshot), preserving /todo's meta/expanded exclusion and abandoned-task annotation as its own logic, and wired a three-way output gate into both commands/todo.md and skill-todo/SKILL.md so an unparseable or silently-failed roadmap can never be reported as a successful annotation pass.

memory_candidates.content: When a shared script (e.g. roadmap-integration.sh) is reused by a caller with narrower requirements than the script's original consumer, a filtered-snapshot pattern lets the caller enforce its own exclusion rules (task_type filtering, status filtering) without widening the shared script: build a scratch state.json containing only the caller-eligible subset, pass it via --state, and rely on the script's own sibling-path resolution (e.g. archive/state.json next to the snapshot) resolving to nothing to scope the run further. This avoids both re-implementing the script's matching logic and bloating the script with caller-specific filters.

When a plan's Overview flags a research report's premise as inaccurate (verified live against the actual repo), that correction must be re-verified during implementation, not just read once: it is easy to accidentally copy the ORIGINAL inaccurate premise into new spec prose while writing plausible-sounding illustrative text, even after having read the correction. A dedicated cross-spec/self-consistency sweep phase (this plan's Phase 6) is what actually caught the defect here, not the initial drafting care.
